answer: Because the horizon index resolves every citation against the sable checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the vertex audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 111 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 111 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
